verdict.rationale: The IRS's own machine channels can carry many items: MeF is a system-to-system XML transmission rail, and IRIS has an Application-to-Application intake for information returns (e.g., 1099s). Both are gated behind credentialed enrollment (Authorized e-file Provider status, a Transmitter Control Code, up to 45-day approval, and fingerprinting for some principals). Bulk is explicitly blocked on other rails: the EIN assistant allows only 1 EIN per responsible party per day, and signed forms require a per-person ID.me biometric login. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of batch/bulk submission volumes, bulk operations outside information returns and e-file, open self-serve programmatic access, and hands-on corroboration of bulk transmission.
